**Cause** (found in `django/db/models/fields/files.py`): `ImageField.contribute_to_class()` unconditionally connected `update_dimension_fields` to the `post_init` signal for every non-abstract model — even when `width_field`/`height_field` were unset, in which case the handler's first check (`has_dimension_fields`) makes it return immediately. Every model instantiation still paid the full signal-dispatch cost for that no-op receiver, which matches the 30–40% init overhead described in the issue.

**Fix** (minimal, source only — no tests touched, nothing committed):
```python
# Only run post-initialization dimension update on non-abstract models
# when dimension fields are used, since the post_init handler is a
# no-op otherwise.
if not cls._meta.abstract and (self.width_field or self.height_field):
    signals.post_init.connect(self.update_dimension_fields, sender=cls)
```
The `ImageFileDescriptor.__set__` path (which passes `force=True`) is untouched, so dimension updates on assignment still work; only the useless signal hookup is skipped.
